solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Learning? This setter's the one to check

parts.note: L is the learner sign, so learning gives L
the setter speaking of themself says I'M, short for 'I am'
IT is the one chosen, as in a game of tag

explanation.surface: A teacher wonders whether education is something the setter should keep an eye on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to check' reads as a verb phrase in the surface; the definition is just 'check', meaning a restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: A check on something is a restraint or cap, the same as a ceiling put upon it.

clue.text: Throws up half of cold milk stew

parts.note: to lob is to throw something high into the air

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of cold

parts.note: to milk is to exploit or use

explanation.surface: Someone vomits after drinking half-cold milk stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Lobscouse is a sailors' meat and vegetable stew, from which the Liverpool word scouse comes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sailors' hash of meat, vegetables and ship's biscuit, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Two family members, one craftsman

parts.note: the two family members are first MA, mother
and second a son, another member of the family

explanation.surface: Two people in one family, one of them a skilled worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two family members' gives two relatives, MA and SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoneworker or builder in stone is a skilled tradesman, a kind of craftsman.

clue.text: Emerge from gate

definitions.meaning: to ... is to come out or emerge
the gate is the number of spectators at a match, an attendance

explanation.walkthrough: A gate in British sport is the crowd attending a game.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrasal verb it means come out; as a noun it is the size of a crowd or attendance.

clue.text: 'In or out?' scene by a volatile old American

definitions.text: 'In or out?' scene by a volatile old American

indicators.note: something volatile is unstable and liable to change, so these letters fly into a new order

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered former American player makes a scene over whether a ball was in or out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: John McEnroe, the volatile American tennis player, shouted this at an umpire over a line call at Wimbledon in 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous protest McEnroe made when disputing an in-or-out line call, so the clue describes the scene exactly.

clue.text: The old country farmer

parts.note: ye is an old way of writing the
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: The former country farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a man owning and working a small estate, a freeholding farmer.

clue.text: United players extremely tense, arrogance at higher level

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: extremely picks the outermost letters of players

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
airs are affected superior manners

explanation.surface: United's players are very tense, their arrogance pitched high.
explanation.definitionFit: On an upper floor of a house is at a higher level than the ground floor.

clue.text: A check on broadcasting charge

indicators.note: broadcasting means the words are given out by voice, so they are taken by sound

parts.note: a rein is a check or restraint, so a check is a rein

explanation.surface: A check on what is broadcast is called for.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone to court to answer a criminal accusation is to charge them formally.

clue.text: 2000-2009 not short of games? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: having enough means not short of something
ties are cup matches, games

explanation.surface: Was the first decade of the century short of games?
explanation.walkthrough: 'not short of games' gives ENOUGH TIES, and 'Not initially' drops the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The decade from 2000 to 2009 is commonly named for the zeros in its years.

clue.text: Form of exercise, turning round and round

indicators.note: turning means the first word for round is turned back

parts.note: a beat is the round a police officer patrols
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A workout of spinning in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fitness system mixing martial-arts kicks and punches with aerobics.

clue.text: See 4
Way in or out, evidently

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words or out evidently, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A door is plainly the way both in and out.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or course taken from one place to another is a way, a synonym.

clue.text: Footballer Butt playing in reserves

parts.note: can is American slang for the buttocks, a butt

indicators.note: in says the playing word goes inside the reserves

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
ON means playing, as in an actor being on

explanation.surface: A footballer surnamed Butt is turning out for the reserve side.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicky Butt was a real Manchester United footballer, which makes 'Butt' look like a name; it is the slang word for backside. Eric Cantona was United's French star.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Cantona is a famous French footballer, an example of the class named.

clue.text: It's a strange laugh, mostly a sneeze

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of it's a are made odd, so they are rearranged
mostly means most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a hoot is a burst of laughter

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that an odd sort of chuckle is really more of a sneeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns IT'S A into ATIS; 'mostly' cuts HOOT to HOO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the word written to represent the sound someone makes when they sneeze, so it stands for one.

clue.text: Subs supply to a sub

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Substitutes are sent to provide cover for another substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb but is read as 'in a supple way', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: German submarines of the world wars are subs, short for submarines; the plural matches.

clue.text: So, rearing ugly head?

indicators.note: ugly suggests the letters are disfigured into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A horrid creature rears its ugly head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearing ugly head' recalls the idiom 'rear its ugly head'; 'head' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The person heading an event or group is the one arranging it, a coordinator.

clue.text: Managed, after pressure, to have control of a meal

indicators.note: after places the managed word behind the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
ran means managed, as in ran a business
a dial is a control knob

explanation.surface: Someone under pressure manages to take charge of a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to a dinner or lunch, as in post-dinner drinks.

clue.text: Future life's starting on farm

indicators.note: starting takes the first letter of life's

parts.note: a grange is a farm with its buildings

explanation.surface: A life of farming lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast covering a long period ahead looks into what is to come.

clue.text: Silesian duchess, good woman wanting drink without the duke

indicators.note: without means outside, so the drink word goes around the rest

parts.note: a swig is a gulp of drink

explanation.surface: A noblewoman goes without a drink because the duke is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside. Hedwig, Duchess of Silesia, became a saint, the 'good woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedwig was a medieval Duchess of Silesia later canonised, a saint and thus a good woman.

clue.text: Say snooker player pots green at first — not the yellow

indicators.note: pots means holds, as a pot holds something, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: EG, for example, is used for say
Jimmy White is a famous English snooker player

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of green

explanation.surface: A snooker player sinks the green first, avoiding the yellow ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say snooker player' is EG WHITE, which takes in G. The definition plays on yellow: the part of an egg that is not the yolk.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear part of an egg surrounds the yellow yolk, so it is the bit that is not the yellow.

clue.text: Sky blocks instalment plan at home — very tight

indicators.note: blocks means fills the space between, so the sky word goes inside

parts.note: HP is hire purchase, a British instalment plan
the air is the sky above
in means at home

explanation.surface: A satellite TV firm stops a home payment scheme that is very tight.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster; HP is hire purchase, buying on instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin bend in a road is a very sharp, tight turn, used as an adjective.

clue.text: Mike's father wants no point of view rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the words no and point of view are read backwards

parts.note: a side of an argument is a point of view

explanation.surface: Someone's dad wants no opinion turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike is short for microphone; Thomas Edison developed the carbon microphone, so he is its father.
explanation.definitionFit: The inventor Thomas Edison developed the carbon microphone, making him the father of the mike in crossword terms.

clue.text: Piece of clothing available in cotton or winceyette?

definitions.meaning: a close-fitting jacket once worn by men
both cotton and winceyette contain a pair of Ts

explanation.surface: Can this garment be bought in cotton or brushed cotton?
explanation.walkthrough: Winceyette is a soft brushed cotton cloth; the second reading splits the answer 6,1 as DOUBLE T.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment is a historical man's jacket; the split reading notes the paired letters in both fabrics.

clue.text: Supply lines training south of the front

indicators.note: south of in a down clue puts the training letters below

parts.note: the prom is the seafront promenade
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: A supply line training exercise behind the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply lines' reads as military logistics but means feeding an actor forgotten words.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed a forgetful actor their words is to give them a cue, supplying lines.

clue.text: Chambers includes new name for Muslim

indicators.note: includes says the set of rooms holds the other letters

parts.note: a suite is a set of rooms, chambers

explanation.surface: The Chambers dictionary adds a new term for a Muslim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' looks like the dictionary but means rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the larger branch of Islam is a member of this group, an example of a Muslim.

clue.text: Man's a crook

definitions.meaning: to man is to provide with workers, to crew
a shepherd's crook is a long stick

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to provide workers for; as a noun, a stick or pole such as a crook.

clue.text: Less precise shape or huge radius

indicators.note: shape as a verb means form into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A geometry question about a less accurate shape or a huge radius.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough estimate is approximate, so a comparatively rough one is not as exact.

clue.text: In jeopardy, having turned evil

indicators.note: turned means the found letters are read backwards
in says the letters are found within jeopardy, having

explanation.surface: Someone in danger has gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: The many-headed monster stands figuratively for a persistent evil that grows when attacked.

clue.text: A model turned author

indicators.note: turned means the word for model is turned around

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A fashion model has become a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek teller of fables is a famous writer, an example of an author.

clue.text: Mayfair doctor tempted to find location further south

parts.note: Mayfair is in the London postcode W1, written here as WI
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
led on means lured or tempted

explanation.surface: A Mayfair doctor is lured to move to a place further south.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is in London's W1 district; this suburb, home of the tennis, is SW19, further south.
explanation.definitionFit: The London suburb lies in the SW19 district, south of central Mayfair, so it is a place further south.

clue.text: Was boxing champion, say, for two weeks

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken and heard by sound, not spelling

parts.note: was boxing is fought, and a champion is a knight, a defender of a cause

explanation.surface: Someone held the boxing title for a couple of weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, without a sounded R, fought sounds like fort.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a contraction of fourteen nights, a period of fourteen days.

clue.text: Find time to meet people

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Someone tries to make time to meet folk.
explanation.definitionFit: To track down or locate a missing thing is to find it, a synonym.
